caption: LUM-1485 terminal title (OSC 0) through the real bridge. Nothing here is visible in the frames on purpose: a window/tab title is terminal state, not cell content, so pages 1-4 are checked by `raw_expect`/`raw_reject` against the byte trace each panel produced. Panel 1 is the automatic title `pi - <cwd>`; panel 2 is `/name demo`, which recomposes it to `pi - demo - <cwd>`; panel 3 is an extension calling `ctx.ui.setTitle` from a slash command (the footer row `handler ran` proves the handler executed); panel 4 is the same call with BEL+ESC inside the title, which must reach the terminal fully neutralised. Commands are sent as two steps — text, a 0.4s pause, then Enter — because a single instantaneous write is classified as a paste burst (LUM-1461) and an Enter inside the burst window is inserted as the paste's trailing newline instead of submitting. Captured with scripts/pty_capture_win.py on Windows 10 (ConPTY), 90x26.

panels.label: 1. startup: the automatic title is `pi - <cwd basename>`

raw_expect.why: upstream's `updateTerminalTitle` composes `APP_TITLE - cwdBasename` when the session has no name (interactive-mode.ts:1017-1028); the harness cwd is a temp dir named pi-pty-cwd-<pid>

reject.why: the title is not cell content: the composed string must never be painted into the grid

expect.why: the TUI is up and idle

panels.label: 2. `/name demo` recomposes the title with the session name in the middle

raw_expect.why: upstream's shape is `APP_TITLE - sessionName - cwdBasename`; `/name` is the Rust path that calls App::set_session_name, which re-queues it

expect.why: the command ran (its info line, not just the echoed prompt)

raw_expect.why: shim -> host_ui_region('setTitle') -> RegionOp::Title -> App -> driver write, byte for byte upstream's OSC 0

expect.why: the same handler's ctx.ui.setStatus is the visible proof it executed; without this row a missing title could be a dispatch failure rather than a broken title channel

reject.why: still not cell content: the driver writes it outside `terminal.draw`

panels.label: 4. a BEL+ESC inside the title is neutralised, not forwarded

raw_expect.why: each control character becomes a space, so the sequence still ends exactly once, where the driver put its BEL

raw_reject.why: the un-sanitised form would let an extension end the title early and start an OSC 2 of its own
the injected control sequence must not survive as an injected control sequence
